answer: Divergence fingerprinting resists Sybil attacks: each identity builds a history of timing, task choices, and counterparties, scored for distinctness from every other identity. A lone honest agent is naturally unique - one violet streak across an atlas of behavior - while a swarm run by one operator leaves correlated fingerprints: identical rhythms, shared counterparties, synchronized pauses. The suspect cluster sits in a low-trust vault until each member proves independent operation. Keeping a thousand fakes uncorrelated costs a thousand distinct operators, so forgery stops scaling.
